{
  "requests": [
    {
      "issue_id": "INDEPENDENT_0",
      "research_question": "What are the alternative pathways by which skeletal muscle contraction terminates and relaxation occurs, specifically when motor neuron ACh release stops versus when ATP depletion/fatigue prevents normal relaxation (rigor)?",
      "required_claim": "Motor neuron cessation of ACh release is the usual trigger for relaxation, but ATP depletion during fatigue can impair Ca2+ reuptake and crossbridge detachment, leading to rigor rather than normal relaxation; thus neuronal-off is not the sole causal route.",
      "biological_scope": "Vertebrate skeletal muscle fibre, excitation-contraction-relaxation cycle, fatigue and rigor",
      "source_preferences": [
        "peer-reviewed physiology textbooks (e.g., Boron & Boulpaep, Guyton & Hall)",
        "review articles on muscle fatigue and rigor",
        "NIH/NCBI Bookshelf physiology resources"
      ],
      "search_queries": [
        "skeletal muscle relaxation mechanisms motor neuron ACh release cessation ATP depletion fatigue rigor",
        "why does ATP depletion prevent skeletal muscle relaxation rigor mortis mechanism",
        "alternative termination of skeletal muscle contraction besides neuronal signal"
      ],
      "expected_evidence_type": "MECHANISM_DESCRIPTION"
    },
    {
      "issue_id": "INDEPENDENT_1",
      "research_question": "When Ca2+ is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) during skeletal muscle excitation, what is the correct subject (sarcoplasm/fibre) and state (elevated cytosolic Ca2+ concentration) that should be represented, rather than attributing the property to the SR itself?",
      "required_claim": "Ca2+ release from the SR raises the Ca2+ concentration in the sarcoplasm (cytosol) of the muscle fibre; the SR is the store, while the sarcoplasm/fibre is the entity whose Ca2+ level becomes elevated.",
      "biological_scope": "Vertebrate skeletal muscle fibre, SR Ca2+ release, cytosolic Ca2+ transient",
      "source_preferences": [
        "peer-reviewed physiology textbooks",
        "review articles on excitation-contraction coupling",
        "NIH/NCBI Bookshelf"
      ],
      "search_queries": [
        "sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release increases cytosolic calcium concentration skeletal muscle excitation contraction coupling",
        "correct anatomical location of elevated calcium during skeletal muscle contraction sarcoplasm versus SR",
        "skeletal muscle calcium transient cytosol SR store"
      ],
      "expected_evidence_type": "MECHANISM_DESCRIPTION"
    },
    {
      "issue_id": "INDEPENDENT_2",
      "research_question": "In the causal chain from SR Ca2+ release to troponin binding, what is the correct source entity for the relation 'Ca2+ binds troponin'? Should the source be the released Ca2+ ion in the sarcoplasm, not the SR?",
      "required_claim": "The Ca2+ that binds troponin is the ion released into the sarcoplasm; the SR is the source/store, not the actor that binds troponin. The relation's source should be sarcoplasmic Ca2+ (or the fibre), not the SR.",
      "biological_scope": "Vertebrate skeletal muscle, Ca2+ binding to troponin C, thin filament regulation",
      "source_preferences": [
        "peer-reviewed physiology textbooks",
        "review articles on thin filament regulation",
        "NIH/NCBI Bookshelf"
      ],
      "search_queries": [
        "calcium binds troponin C skeletal muscle sarcoplasmic calcium source not SR",
        "troponin calcium binding step excitation contraction coupling source of calcium",
        "thin filament regulation calcium troponin tropomyosin skeletal muscle mechanism"
      ],
      "expected_evidence_type": "MECHANISM_DESCRIPTION"
    },
    {
      "issue_id": "INDEPENDENT_3",
      "research_question": "In the crossbridge cycle, what are the correct roles of the regulatory complex (troponin-tropomyosin) and the contractile filaments (actin-myosin)? Does the observable 'contraction requires Ca2+ and ATP' correctly map to the relation of myosin heads binding actin sites, rather than misassigning the regulatory complex as the source actor?",
      "required_claim": "The crossbridge cycle involves myosin heads binding to actin filament sites; troponin-tropomyosin regulates exposure of those sites. Ca2+ and ATP are required, but the relation's source should be myosin (or the thick filament), not the regulatory complex.",
      "biological_scope": "Vertebrate skeletal muscle, crossbridge cycle, actin-myosin interaction, regulation by troponin-tropomyosin",
      "source_preferences": [
        "peer-reviewed physiology textbooks",
        "review articles on crossbridge cycle",
        "NIH/NCBI Bookshelf"
      ],
      "search_queries": [
        "crossbridge cycle myosin head binds actin role of troponin tropomyosin calcium ATP skeletal muscle",
        "correct actors in actin myosin crossbridge formation regulatory complex versus contractile filaments",
        "observable contraction requires calcium and ATP relation to myosin actin binding"
      ],
      "expected_evidence_type": "MECHANISM_DESCRIPTION"
    },
    {
      "issue_id": "INDEPENDENT_4",
      "research_question": "What is the correct subject for the states 'actin sites shielded/unshielded'? Is it the actin myosin-binding site (on actin) that becomes exposed, rather than the troponin-tropomyosin complex itself being the subject of shielding/unshielding?",
      "required_claim": "Tropomyosin covers the myosin-binding sites on actin; Ca2+ binding to troponin causes tropomyosin to move, exposing those actin sites. The shielded/unshielded object is the actin site, not the regulatory complex.",
      "biological_scope": "Vertebrate skeletal muscle, thin filament regulation, actin-myosin binding site exposure",
      "source_preferences": [
        "peer-reviewed physiology textbooks",
        "review articles on thin filament regulation",
        "NIH/NCBI Bookshelf"
      ],
      "search_queries": [
        "tropomyosin blocks myosin binding sites on actin calcium troponin exposes actin sites skeletal muscle",
        "subject of shielded unshielded actin binding sites troponin tropomyosin complex",
        "thin filament regulation actin site exposure by tropomyosin movement"
      ],
      "expected_evidence_type": "MECHANISM_DESCRIPTION"
    }
  ],
  "candidate_urls": [
    "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537139/",
    "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK556013/"
  ],
  "scientific_queries": [
    "vertebrate skeletal muscle excitation contraction relaxation mechanism calcium troponin tropomyosin crossbridge ATP fatigue rigor alternative termination"
  ]
}
